title: Password-reset token consumption and password update are not atomic
detail: The function reads a live unused token,updates users.password_hash,then marks password_resets.used in a separate update. There is no token-state compare-and-set claim or shared transaction across these operations.
impact: Concurrent reuse or a failure between writes can permit a token to remain usable or competing resets to overwrite the password. This is a source-derived race/failure concern;no exploit or reset was attempted.
recommendation: In a separately approved fix,use one transactional conditional token-consumption/password-update flow with expiry checks and failure recovery;add isolated concurrency/rollback tests.
test: test_functional_blockers_regression.py; password-reset contracts in existing suites do not establish concurrent one-time consumption.

title: Seven-day access JWTs have no server-side session/password-version revocation
detail: Tokens carry sub,role,email,type,exp;authorization reloads DB roles,which is positive,but no session ID/token version/password-changed cutoff is checked. Password reset does not revoke existing access JWTs. No logout-all/revoke endpoint found in179 registrations.
impact: A previously obtained valid token can retain access until expiry after a password change,unless the account is removed or other checks deny it. Native/client logout alone does not revoke a copied token.
recommendation: Agree on session-revocation policy;then add server-checked token version/session state and invalidate sessions on sensitive account changes without weakening role checks.
test: test_frontend_contracts.py;source/session inventory;no new token test executed.

title: IP rate-limit identity trusts caller-supplied X-Forwarded-For
detail: The first forwarded header value is accepted without an application trusted-proxy check. A sanitizing ingress may mitigate this,but actual ingress configuration is unavailable.
impact: If directly reachable or behind an unsanitized proxy,IP-based registration/reset/login throttles can be evaded. Email/subject counters still provide separate protection where used.
recommendation: Verify trusted proxy/ingress behavior;derive client identity only from trusted forwarding information and retain subject controls.
test: Source inspection only;no spoofing requests or bypass attempts performed.

title: Authentication throttle check and increment are separate operations
detail: A request reads counters before later $inc;concurrent requests can all pass the same limit check. Login increments only after failed verification.
impact: Burst concurrency may exceed the intended per-window limit. No concurrency/abuse attack was run.
recommendation: Use a reviewed atomic limiting primitive with shared worker semantics and explicit rejection policy;test only on an isolated service.
test: Existing auth tests show basic rate behavior historically,not strict burst-cap enforcement.

title: Legacy diagnostic status endpoint permits anonymous persistent writes
detail: POST /api/status directly inserts client_name into status_checks without auth or endpoint rate control;client_name has no explicit length bound. GET returns up to1000 records. Global ingress controls are unverified.
impact: Untrusted callers can create diagnostic data/storage load and retrieve the shared diagnostic feed. This is legacy behavior,not assumed to be intentional public operational policy.
recommendation: Owner should decide whether to retire,restrict or bound this legacy endpoint;require suitable authorization/rate/size controls before production. Do not remove it during audit.
test: Static route/body inspection;no diagnostic record created.

title: Password character limits exceed bcrypt byte limit
detail: Registration permits128 characters and reset128,while hash_password passes UTF-8 directly to bcrypt4.1.3. No explicit72-byte bound or reviewed long-password handling is present.
impact: bcrypt byte truncation/compatibility can make distinct long inputs equivalent or otherwise cause password-contract ambiguity. Exact runtime behavior was not exercised;do not report a tested credential collision.
recommendation: Review byte-aware password policy/library behavior and provide compatible migration/tests rather than silently truncating credentials.
test: SOURCE VERIFIED configuration mismatch;runtime UNVERIFIED;no passwords/salts/credentials created.

title: Blocking provider HTTP inside async payment routes
detail: Synchronous requests/http_requests calls appear in async handlers with timeouts. Real-provider latency/load behavior is not verified.
impact: Slow provider responses can occupy the event loop and reduce availability;this is a source-level performance/availability concern,not a measured outage.
recommendation: After approval,review bounded async HTTP or safe thread offload while keeping all provider effects outside retried DB callbacks and preserving idempotency.

title: Webhook size check occurs after whole request body is buffered
detail: The route awaits request.body(),computes HMAC,then event_payload checks1MiB. The check does not bound the earlier body read. Production ingress body-size protection is unknown.
impact: When the provider route is configured,oversized unauthenticated bodies can consume buffering/HMAC resources before rejection. This was not load-tested and no large request was sent.
recommendation: Review ingress caps and an endpoint streaming/body cap before full buffering,while preserving exact raw bytes for signature validation.
test: Source inspection;test_webhook_envelope_security.py checks parser bounds,not pre-buffer transport allocation.
